import pandas as pd

# Load all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column

# Source 0
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_34/training_0.csv"
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)

# Source 1
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_34/training_1.csv"
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Source 2
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_34/training_2.csv"
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)

# Source 3
source3_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_34/training_3.csv"
df3 = pd.read_csv(source3_path, index_col=0)

# Source 4
source4_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_34/training_4.csv"
df4 = pd.read_csv(source4_path, index_col=0)

# Source 5
source5_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_34/training_5.csv"
df5 = pd.read_csv(source5_path, index_col=0)

# Source 6
source6_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_34/training_6.csv"
df6 = pd.read_csv(source6_path, index_col=0)

# According to operation_history, perform joins in the given sequence on 'fips_code'

# 1) JOIN : [["Source6_34_3","Source6_34_5"],["fips_code","fips_code"]]
df_3_5 = pd.merge(df3, df5, on="fips_code", how="inner", suffixes=('_x', '_y'))

# 2) JOIN : [["Source6_34_2","Source6_34_6"],["fips_code","fips_code"]]
df_2_6 = pd.merge(df2, df6, on="fips_code", how="inner", suffixes=('_x', '_y'))

# 3) JOIN : [["Source6_34_0","Source6_34_1"],["fips_code","fips_code"]]
df_0_1 = pd.merge(df0, df1, on="fips_code", how="inner")

# 4) JOIN : [["Source6_34_1","Source6_34_4"],["fips_code","fips_code"]]
df_1_4 = pd.merge(df1, df4, on="fips_code", how="inner", suffixes=('_x', '_y'))

# 5) JOIN : [["Source6_34_3","Source6_34_2"],["fips_code","fips_code"]]
df_3_2 = pd.merge(df3, df2, on="fips_code", how="inner", suffixes=('_x', '_y'))

# Now we need to combine these intermediate results to get the final target table.
# The target schema has many columns from different sources, and the joins above overlap.
# We must join all sources on 'fips_code' to get all columns.

# Strategy:
# - Start from df3 (main demographic and labor force info)
# - Join df5 (geographic and population info) => done as df_3_5
# - Join df2 (diabetes info) and df6 (inactivity info) => done as df_2_6
# - Join df0 and df1 (unions_count and drug_deaths) => df_0_1
# - Join df4 (gun_store_counts) with df1 => df_1_4
# - Join df3 and df2 => df_3_2

# We have these partial joins, but to get all columns in one dataframe, we join them all on fips_code.

# Join df_3_5 with df_2_6 on fips_code
df_3_5_2_6 = pd.merge(df_3_5, df_2_6.drop(columns=['state_x', 'fips_code', 'county_x', 'county_y', 'state_y']), 
                      left_on='fips_code', right_on='fips_code', how='inner')

# Join the above with df_0_1 on fips_code
df_3_5_2_6_0_1 = pd.merge(df_3_5_2_6, df_0_1.drop(columns=['fips_code']), left_on='fips_code', right_index=True, how='inner')

# Join df_1_4 (gun_store_counts) with df_3_5_2_6_0_1 on fips_code
df_1_4_reduced = df_1_4[['fips_code', 'gun_store_counts']]
df_all = pd.merge(df_3_5_2_6_0_1, df_1_4_reduced, on='fips_code', how='inner')

# Now, ensure all columns in target schema are present and properly named

# Target schema columns:
target_columns = [
    'state_x', 'statefp', 'countyfp', 'county_name_x', 'fips_code', 'winning_party', 'State', 'Area_name',
    'Civilian_labor_force_2012', 'Employed_2012', 'Unemployed_2012', 'Unemployment_rate_2012',
    'state_y', 'ansi_code', 'county_name_y', 'population', 'housing_units', 'area_land_mt', 'area_water_mt',
    'area_land_mi', 'area_water_mi', 'latitude', 'logitude', 'naics', 'unions_count', 'state_x_25', 'county_x',
    'diabetes_count', 'diabetes%', 'state_y_29', 'county_y', 'inactivity_count', 'inactivity%', 'county_name',
    'drug_deaths', 'gun_store_counts'
]

# Some columns need to be created or renamed to match target schema exactly.

# Rename columns from df_all to match target schema:

# From df3 (suffix _x):
# 'state' -> 'state_x'
# 'county_name' -> 'county_name_x'
# 'state' (from df5) -> 'state_y'
# 'county_name' (from df5) -> 'county_name_y'
# 'state' (from df2) -> 'state_x_25' (from df2 is 'state')
# 'county' (from df2) -> 'county_x'
# 'state' (from df6) -> 'state_y_29'
# 'county' (from df6) -> 'county_y'
# 'county_name' (from df1) -> 'county_name'
# 'logitude' is misspelled in source, keep as is

# Rename columns accordingly:

df_all.rename(columns={
    # From df3 (original columns, suffix _x)
    'state_x': 'state_x',
    'statefp': 'statefp',
    'countyfp': 'countyfp',
    'county_name_x': 'county_name_x',
    'fips_code': 'fips_code',
    'winning_party': 'winning_party',
    'State': 'State',
    'Area_name': 'Area_name',
    'Civilian_labor_force_2012': 'Civilian_labor_force_2012',
    'Employed_2012': 'Employed_2012',
    'Unemployed_2012': 'Unemployed_2012',
    'Unemployment_rate_2012': 'Unemployment_rate_2012',

    # From df5 (suffix _y)
    'state_y': 'state_y',
    'ansi_code': 'ansi_code',
    'county_name_y': 'county_name_y',
    'population': 'population',
    'housing_units': 'housing_units',
    'area_land_mt': 'area_land_mt',
    'area_water_mt': 'area_water_mt',
    'area_land_mi': 'area_land_mi',
    'area_water_mi': 'area_water_mi',
    'latitude': 'latitude',
    'logitude': 'logitude',

    # From df0
    'naics': 'naics',
    'unions_count': 'unions_count',

    # From df2 (diabetes and state/county rename)
    'state_x': 'state_x_25',  # from df2 'state' renamed to 'state_x_25'
    'county_x': 'county_x',
    'diabetes_count': 'diabetes_count',
    'diabetes%': 'diabetes%',

    # From df6 (inactivity and state/county rename)
    'state_y': 'state_y_29',  # from df6 'state' renamed to 'state_y_29'
    'county_y': 'county_y',
    'inactivity_count': 'inactivity_count',
    'inactivity%': 'inactivity%',

    # From df1 (drug_deaths and county_name)
    'county_name': 'county_name',
    'drug_deaths': 'drug_deaths',

    # From df_1_4 (gun_store_counts) already merged as 'gun_store_counts'
}, inplace=True)

# After renaming, some columns from df2 and df6 have conflicting names with df3 and df5 columns.
# We must assign these columns explicitly from df2 and df6 before merging to avoid overwriting.

# To fix this, we will re-merge df2 and df6 with suffixes to keep their columns distinct before final merge.

# Re-merge df3 and df5 (df_3_5)
df_3_5 = pd.merge(df3, df5, on="fips_code", how="inner", suffixes=('_x', '_y'))

# Rename df2 columns to target names for diabetes and state_x_25, county_x
df2_renamed = df2.rename(columns={
    'state': 'state_x_25',
    'county': 'county_x',
    'diabetes_count': 'diabetes_count',
    'diabetes%': 'diabetes%'
})

# Rename df6 columns to target names for inactivity and state_y_29, county_y
df6_renamed = df6.rename(columns={
    'state': 'state_y_29',
    'county': 'county_y',
    'inactivity_count': 'inactivity_count',
    'inactivity%': 'inactivity%'
})

# Merge df2_renamed and df6_renamed on fips_code
df_2_6 = pd.merge(df2_renamed, df6_renamed, on='fips_code', how='inner')

# Merge df_3_5 with df_2_6 on fips_code
df_3_5_2_6 = pd.merge(df_3_5, df_2_6, on='fips_code', how='inner')

# Merge df0 and df1 on fips_code
df_0_1 = pd.merge(df0, df1, on='fips_code', how='inner')

# Merge df1 and df4 on fips_code to get gun_store_counts
df_1_4 = pd.merge(df1, df4, on='fips_code', how='inner')

# Merge df_3_5_2_6 with df_0_1 on fips_code
df_all = pd.merge(df_3_5_2_6, df_0_1[['fips_code', 'naics', 'unions_count', 'drug_deaths', 'county_name']], on='fips_code', how='inner')

# Merge df_all with gun_store_counts from df_1_4
df_all = pd.merge(df_all, df_1_4[['fips_code', 'gun_store_counts']], on='fips_code', how='inner')

# Now select and reorder columns to match target schema exactly
df_final = df_all[[
    'state_x', 'statefp', 'countyfp', 'county_name_x', 'fips_code', 'winning_party', 'State', 'Area_name',
    'Civilian_labor_force_2012', 'Employed_2012', 'Unemployed_2012', 'Unemployment_rate_2012',
    'state_y', 'ansi_code', 'county_name_y', 'population', 'housing_units', 'area_land_mt', 'area_water_mt',
    'area_land_mi', 'area_water_mi', 'latitude', 'logitude', 'naics', 'unions_count', 'state_x_25', 'county_x',
    'diabetes_count', 'diabetes%', 'state_y_29', 'county_y', 'inactivity_count', 'inactivity%', 'county_name',
    'drug_deaths', 'gun_store_counts'
]]

# Ensure data types match target schema

# Convert integer columns
int_cols = [
    'statefp', 'countyfp', 'fips_code', 'ansi_code', 'population', 'housing_units',
    'area_land_mt', 'area_water_mt', 'naics', 'unions_count', 'diabetes_count',
    'inactivity_count', 'drug_deaths', 'gun_store_counts'
]
for col in int_cols:
    df_final[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_final[col], errors='coerce').fillna(0).astype(int)

# Convert float columns
float_cols = ['Unemployment_rate_2012', 'area_land_mi', 'area_water_mi', 'latitude', 'logitude', 'diabetes%', 'inactivity%']
for col in float_cols:
    df_final[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_final[col], errors='coerce').astype(float)

# Convert string columns
str_cols = [
    'state_x', 'county_name_x', 'winning_party', 'State', 'Area_name', 'state_y',
    'county_name_y', 'state_x_25', 'county_x', 'state_y_29', 'county_y', 'county_name'
]
for col in str_cols:
    df_final[col] = df_final[col].astype(str)

# Write the final dataframe to CSV
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_34/target_multisource.csv"
df_final.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

# Join Source6_34_3 and Source6_34_5 on fips_code
df = pd.merge(source3, source5, on="fips_code", how="inner")

# Join the above with Source6_34_2 on fips_code
df = pd.merge(df, source2, on="fips_code", how="inner", suffixes=('', '_y2'))

# Join the above with Source6_34_6 on fips_code
df = pd.merge(df, source6, on="fips_code", how="inner", suffixes=('', '_y6'))

# Join the above with Source6_34_1 on fips_code
df = pd.merge(df, source1, on="fips_code", how="inner", suffixes=('', '_y1'))

# Join Source6_34_1 and Source6_34_4 on fips_code to get gun_store_counts aligned with drug_deaths

df = pd.merge(df, source0, on="fips_code", how="inner")

# Rename columns to match target schema exactly
df.rename(columns={
    'state_x': 'state_x',
    'statefp': 'statefp',
    'countyfp': 'countyfp',
    'county_name_x': 'county_name_x',

    'county': 'county_x',   # from source2 'county' renamed to 'county_x'
    'diabetes_count': 'diabetes_count',
    'diabetes%': 'diabetes%',

    'inactivity_count': 'inactivity_count',

    'drug_deaths': 'drug_deaths',

}, inplace=True)

# The columns 'state_x_25', 'county_x' come from source2's 'state' and 'county'
# The columns 'state_y_29', 'county_y' come from source6's 'state' and 'county'
# The 'county_name' column is from source1's 'county_name' (already present)

# Group by all leftmost non-float unique columns in target schema (all except aggregations)
group_by_cols = [
    'state_x', 'statefp', 'countyfp', 'county_name_x', 'fips_code', 'winning_party', 'State', 'Area_name',

]

# Aggregate sum for count columns (unions_count, diabetes_count, inactivity_count, drug_deaths, gun_store_counts)
agg_dict = {

    'diabetes_count': 'sum',
    'inactivity_count': 'sum',
    'drug_deaths': 'sum',

    'inactivity_count', 'inactivity%', 'county_name', 'drug_deaths', 'gun_store_counts'
]

# Some columns like 'diabetes%' and 'inactivity%' are not aggregated, so take first value per group

non_agg_cols = ['diabetes%', 'inactivity%']
